notes: Each run starts from a scaffolded nextjs-bootstrap project (has ARCHITECTURE.md + MODULE_REGISTRY.md + shared form/typography/overlay components). Eval 3 specifically pre-seeds a feature-local component to test the dedup/move behavior. Baseline (without_skill) gets the same starting project + prompt, no skill. Replace <FIGMA_LINK>/<FRAME_LINK> with live node-specific Figma URLs before running.

evals.name: frame-to-components-placement
evals.prompt: Turn this Figma frame into Next.js components: <FRAME_LINK>. It's a landing page section with a header, a hero, and a row of cards. Build it out properly for our project.
evals.expected_output: Header and Hero created in components/shared (layout/marketing groups), Card as a shared data-display component with variants (not one card per item); page/template composes them; Tailwind utilities + theme tokens (no raw hex/px); shadcn primitives composed not duplicated; new shared components registered in MODULE_REGISTRY.md; build passes.

evals.name: reuse-existing-shared
evals.prompt: Build this profile screen from <FRAME_LINK>. Heads up — we already have a shared Avatar and Card in the project, reuse those, don't make new ones.
evals.expected_output: Existing shared Avatar and Card are imported and reused (no new Avatar/Card files); only genuinely new pieces are created; if the design needs an avatar variant (e.g. status dot) it extends the existing component via a prop/cva variant rather than forking; registry not polluted with duplicates.

evals.name: dedup-move-to-shared
evals.prompt: Implement this dashboard frame: <FRAME_LINK>. It reuses the same StatCard that already exists inside the billing feature, but now the analytics feature needs it too.
evals.expected_output: StatCard is MOVED from features/billing/components to components/shared/data-display (not copied), billing's imports updated, registry row added; the new analytics screen imports the now-shared StatCard; no duplicate StatCard left in billing.
